statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is low, while Stress remains extreme.
recommendation: Tail remains below the watch threshold. The current evidence is mixed: delayed NQ quotes are modestly positive, while Broadcom guidance and the U.S.-Iran/oil backdrop preserve high event sensitivity.
headline: Low Tail risk with extreme event stress ahead of the September 3 U.S. data cluster
body: A delayed public NQ reference near 29,145 is modestly above the 29,125.5 prior settle, but the quoted data are delayed and do not establish persistent one-way structure. Broadcom’s Q4 revenue guide drew a negative after-hours reaction, while renewed U.S.-Iran fighting and impaired Hormuz traffic keep energy and rates transmission risk elevated.

sources.title: Reuters — Oil settles 1% higher as U.S.-Iran strikes threaten supplies

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 UTC clock hours, published Tail ranged from 18% to 31%. Elevated orange states appeared during several European and pre-U.S. hours, then eased to green from 16:00 through 20:00 UTC before the Broadcom event returned the state to watch at 21:00 and 23:00 UTC. The 22:00 UTC slot has no published assessment.
outlookSummary: The next concentrated risk window is 12:15-14:45 UTC on September 3 around trade and productivity data, the U.S. cash open and ISM Services. Forecast Tail remains at or below 24% before those outcomes because event importance alone is not evidence of a persistent path; later changes depend on observed continuation, retracement quality and cross-asset alignment.

forecast.analysis: Delayed public NQ quotes are modestly above the prior settle, but quote dispersion and delay prevent a claim of persistent one-way structure. Broadcom’s softer revenue guide and the Hormuz/oil shock keep event stress extreme while Tail remains below the watch threshold.
drivers: Delayed NQ quotes modestly above prior settle

Broadcom forecasts quarterly sales below estimates amid rising custom AI chip competition

forecast.analysis: If overnight NQ remains two-sided and retracements continue to appear, Tail would stay low; a clean extension toward new session extremes without pullbacks would be the main reason for reassessment.

During thin Asian-session liquidity, the baseline remains mixed unless NQ begins repeated directional extension. Oil and rates remain conditional amplifiers rather than proof of mean-reversion failure.
With no scheduled U.S. catalyst in this hour, risk would ease toward normal if futures hold a balanced range; a geopolitical headline or abrupt yield move could reintroduce whipsaw risk.
Pre-Europe conditions would remain lower-Tail if price discovery stays rotational. A fresh Hormuz escalation combined with aligned rates and technology weakness would raise the path risk.
As Europe approaches, cross-asset direction could become more informative. Tail would remain low unless NQ follows any oil/rates impulse with shallow pullbacks and repeated extension.
European participation may widen ranges. A mixed equity response with retracements would keep Tail low, while synchronized NQ weakness, higher yields and stronger volatility would raise it.
European cash trading can sharpen cross-asset signals. Tail stays low in the forecast unless directional efficiency rises and NQ begins holding near an extreme with failed retracements.
Approaching the U.S. premarket, Broadcom’s post-earnings read-through may regain influence. A contained semiconductor reaction would limit Tail; broad technology alignment would increase it.
Premarket liquidity is expected to deepen. Risk remains below watch unless NQ develops sustained extension while yields or oil move in the same adverse direction.

One hour before the 12:30 UTC data cluster, uncertainty rises. Event importance lifts Stress, but Tail reaches watch only as a conditional allowance for possible pre-release positioning and thin retracements.
The final pre-release hour carries concentrated gap and headline risk. Tail is forecast at watch, not block, because the release outcomes and subsequent price path are still unobserved.

Trade and revised productivity data are scheduled for 12:30 UTC. Tail is capped at watch before outcomes are known; a block would require observed post-release persistence, shallow pullbacks or aligned cross-asset extension.
The U.S. cash open follows the 12:30 UTC releases. Whipsaw risk stays extreme; Tail remains watch unless opening-auction direction persists through failed retracements and holds near an extreme.

ISM Services is scheduled for 14:00 UTC. This is the peak conditional risk hour: Tail remains watch pre-outcome, while any later escalation would depend on the observed NQ path and rates/volatility confirmation.

After the data/open sequence, Tail would begin to fall if price discovery becomes two-sided and volatility decays. Persistent extension through the first post-ISM retracement would keep risk elevated.

By late morning U.S. time, the forecast shifts toward mixed conditions if earlier shocks are being retraced. Tail stays at watch only while delayed second-leg risk from rates or technology remains plausible.
Mid-session Tail would return to low if NQ is no longer holding an extreme and cross-assets stabilize. A renewed same-direction move in yields, oil and semiconductors would invalidate that easing.
Early afternoon is forecast as mixed rather than directional. Tail remains low unless a fresh catalyst produces repeated extension with poor retracement quality.

Power-hour conditions can amplify late-session moves. Tail rises to watch conditionally if the day’s dominant direction reasserts with breadth and technology participation; otherwise the baseline remains two-sided.

Into the U.S. cash close, Tail would ease if late moves retrace and closing flows remain orderly. A close pinned at an extreme after repeated extensions would argue for higher risk in the next assessment.
After the cash close, lower participation normally reduces directional confirmation. Tail is forecast low unless a company or geopolitical headline creates a new discontinuity.
At the evening futures transition, liquidity can be uneven. Tail remains low unless the reopened market gaps and continues in one direction without meaningful retracement.
Late evening risk is forecast mixed. With the next major U.S. labor release still beyond this horizon, Tail would stay low absent a new geopolitical or cross-asset alignment.
